title: fix(runtime): every door that starts a flow by name refuses a record key the caller cannot read before the run exists
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-steve"} -->
_Requested by **Steve** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01FdL1XeUyvVNxLreh3F4Qi9?thread=cmsg_01FdL1XeUyvVNxLreh3F4Qi9Wc1DX7AbpEoxwZbBojqqdW)_
Fixes #29050

Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么：所有按名字启动 flow 的入口（两种写法的 trigger 路由、声明式 `type: 'flow'` endpoint、flow 类 action 的 REST 与 MCP 入口）在启动前，都用调用者自己的权限读一次这次启动交给运行的记录；读不到就回 action 入口同一个 `404 RECORD_NOT_FOUND`，不产生运行记录。
- 为什么改：三个入口对「这次启动指向的记录，调用者能不能读」问法不一致，action 入口问了，其余入口没问；以 `runAs: 'system'` 运行的 flow 会越过调用者自己的读权限。本 PR 让三个入口问同一个问题、给同一个答复。
- 风险与回滚：调用者能读的记录、不指定记录的启动、系统身份（进程内调用方）都不变。新增三种拒绝：读不到或不存在的记录回 404；以系统身份运行的 flow 指定了记录但没指定对象回 400；记录键不是单个 id 回 400。用户身份 flow 在指定了对象时也会检查，与 action 入口一致。回滚即撤掉本 PR。
- 先看：`packages/runtime/src/action-execution.ts` 的 `refuseUnreadableFlowStartRecords` 和 `flowActionCallerRecordKeys`；`domains/automation.ts` 的 `respondToFlowTrigger` 与 `flowStartRecordKeys`；`endpoint-executor.ts` 的 `executeFlow`。
- 两分钟验证：`pnpm --filter @objectstack/runtime exec vitest run src/flow-start-record-admission.test.ts`，应看到 32 条全过。
- 需要你做的：无，席位落地。

## What changes

Every door that starts a flow by name now asks a third admission question after `flowStartRefusal` and before `execute()`: **the row this start addresses.** One function, `refuseUnreadableFlowStartRecords` (`packages/runtime/src/action-execution.ts`, beside the action door's subject load that it reuses), is called by:

- the trigger routes, `POST /api/v1/automation/:name/trigger` and the legacy `POST /api/v1/automation/trigger/:name` (`respondToFlowTrigger`, `domains/automation.ts`);
- a declared endpoint of `type: 'flow'` (`executeFlow`, `endpoint-executor.ts`);
- an action of `type: 'flow'` at the REST action route and the MCP `run_action` tool (`dispatchFlowAction`), for the row slots the caller's own `params` fill. The routed record keeps the subject load and refusal it already had, unchanged.

The rule it applies:

- **Which keys.** Every record key in a row slot the door itself defines (`recordId`, the `{objectName}Id` alias, an action's declared `recordIdParam`), with the value the run will receive, a caller's own `params` value included.
- **The load.** Each key is loaded in the caller's own scope through the door's own caller-scope read (`callData('get', …)`, the read the action door's subject load makes), via `loadActionSubjectRecord`.
- **The refusal.** A key that scope does not deliver is refused by `refuseDeniedSubjectLoad`: the action door's own `404 RECORD_NOT_FOUND` (ADR-0112 envelope). An unreadable record and an id that names nothing get one answer. Nothing runs and no run is persisted.
- **The object.** The object the start names: `objectName` (or `object`) in a trigger or endpoint body, the action's own object at the action door. A start that names a record key but no object cannot be judged: a flow declared `runAs: 'system'` refuses it `400 VALIDATION_FAILED` naming `objectName`; a flow that runs as the user starts as before.
- **Non-id keys.** A record key whose value is not one id (a string or a number) is refused `400 VALIDATION_FAILED` naming the key, and is never loaded.
- **Unchanged.** A start whose caller can read the record; a start that names no record; the system principal; an action whose `recordIdField` names a field other than `id` (its row slots carry that field's value, not an id).

Supporting changes:

- `flow-start-admission.ts`: the module docblock states the third question, and `flowRunsElevated` is the one reading of `runAs` it needs. The module still imports nothing from `action-execution.ts`.
- `domains/automation.ts`: `recordIdAlias` is now the one spelling of the `{objectName}Id` alias, read by `buildAutomationContext` to seed it and by the new `flowStartRecordKeys` to judge it. The trigger routes answer the refusal through `deps.errorFromThrown`, the exit the action door serves the same refusal through, so both doors answer one envelope.
- `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx`: row 57 (the flow start admission bypass of the system principal) now names this check and its symbol, and the site register is regenerated with `check-system-context-census.mjs --write`. The new function reads `isSystem` once, so `check:system-context-census` required a row to own it.
- Changeset: `.changeset/29050-flow-start-record-admission.md`, a `patch` for `@objectstack/runtime`, rule-only.

## Why

#29050: the doors that start a flow by name did not all ask whether the caller can read the record the start hands the run, so the three doors disagreed. `flow-start-admission.ts` already says a door left out of a start rule is the defect. This PR states the rule once and has every door ask it.

## Tests

- **New** `packages/runtime/src/flow-start-record-admission.test.ts` (32 tests), over a row-scoped data double:
  - at both trigger spellings, a flow endpoint, the REST action route and the MCP action tool, a start door given a record key the caller cannot read is refused `404 RECORD_NOT_FOUND`, and no run is created;
  - a record that does not exist gets the identical answer;
  - a start on a record the caller can read starts the run (the firing control at each door);
  - each row slot is judged with the value the run receives;
  - an elevated start that names a record but no object is refused 400 naming `objectName`, and nothing is loaded;
  - a record key that is not one id is refused 400 naming the key, and nothing is loaded;
  - unchanged cases: no record key, the system principal, a user-run flow with no object, an action whose row slots carry a non-id field;
  - the trigger route and the action door answer the same status, code and message for the same refusal.
- **Forced test edits** (8 files). Each fixture started a flow on a record against a data double that did not serve that record to the caller. Each now serves it; no assertion changed:
  - `flow-run-locale.test.ts`, `flow-run-posture.test.ts`, `flow-caller-param-keys.test.ts`: the trigger-route cases' kernel also serves a data read for the launched record.
  - `domains/automation-trigger-params-shape.test.ts`: the dispatcher double also serves the launched record (the `a record launch` case).
  - `domain-handler-registry.test.ts`: the both-routes identity case serves its launched record.
  - `endpoint-executor.test.ts`: the flow delegation case's `callData` double returns the launched record.
  - `dispatcher-plugin.endpoint-fallback.integration.test.ts`: the fake engine serves the row the flow endpoint is launched on.
  - `http-dispatcher.actions-type-dispatch.test.ts`: in `lets an explicit param win over every seeded key`, the caller can also read the record its own param names.

## Acceptance notes

- **Doors measured** (the card's assumption A). Four entrances reach `IAutomationService.execute` by flow name from a caller: the two trigger spellings, a declared `type: 'flow'` endpoint, and `dispatchFlowAction` (shared by the REST action route and the MCP `run_action` tool). All four now ask the question. A parent flow's `subflow` node starts its child through the engine, not a door, as `flow-start-admission.ts` already notes.
- **The object** (assumption B). The trigger and endpoint bodies carry `objectName`/`object`, and the action door has its action's object. A record key with no object is refused for an elevated flow and passes for a user flow, as described above. No `packages/spec` change.
- **User-run flows** (assumption C). The check also runs for user flows when the start names an object, the same way the action door's routed-record load already runs for every flow. Measured cost: 12 existing tests in 8 files had to serve their launched record (the forced edits above).
- **Before any run.** Every refusal is asserted with `execute` never called.

## Verification

Head `2020b6e5`. Code readings were taken on `5fda11a5` (the merge of `origin/main` at `4550091a`); `2020b6e5` adds only the docs row above. Heavy runs went through `os-verify-lock.sh`.

<details><summary>Runtime package: typecheck, full test, lint</summary>

- `pnpm --workspace-concurrency=2 --filter '@objectstack/runtime^...' build` after the merge: VERDICT command-exit 0.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/runtime typecheck` (includes `check:test-typecheck`): VERDICT command-exit 0.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/runtime test`: Test Files 515 passed (515), Tests 8350 passed, 19 skipped (8369). VERDICT command-exit 0.
- Before the fixture edits, the same full run read Test Files 8 failed, 507 passed (515); Tests 12 failed, 8338 passed. All 12 were the record launches named under *Forced test edits*, failing with `expected 404 to be 200`, an `execute` mock called 0 times, or (the action door case) a run that never started.
- `vitest run` over the 8 edited files plus the new file: Test Files 9 passed (9), Tests 250 passed (250).
- `eslint packages/runtime --no-inline-config` (the root `pnpm lint` command, scoped): exit 0, no output.

</details>

<details><summary>Ablations: every new refusal goes red when the check is taken out</summary>

Each leg used `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` on one anchor, ran `vitest run src/flow-start-record-admission.test.ts` through the lock, and restored. `git diff HEAD` was 0 bytes after every leg.

- **Trigger routes** (the trigger door hands the check no keys): 17 failed, 15 passed. For example, `expected 200 to be 404`, `expected 200 to be 400`, and the parity case `expected { status: 200, … } to deeply equal { status: 404, … }`.
- **Flow endpoint** (no keys): 1 failed (`a record key the caller cannot read: 404 RECORD_NOT_FOUND, no run`): `expected 200 to be 404`.
- **Action door** (no caller-param keys): 3 failed (REST ×2, MCP): `expected 200 to be 404`, and `promise resolved "{ ok: true, … }" instead of rejecting`.
- **No object on an elevated flow** (always start): 2 failed: `expected 200 to be 400`.
- **Non-id key** (loaded instead of refused): 2 failed: `expected 404 to be 400`.
- **The `{object}Id` slot** (dropped from the keys): 2 failed: `expected 200 to be 404`.

</details>

<details><summary>dispatch-gates</summary>

- `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` on `2020b6e5`: 93 commands. Each ran with stdin closed after a full `turbo run build --filter='./packages/**'` (Tasks 78 successful, 78 total; VERDICT command-exit 0). All 93 exited 0, `check:nul-bytes` included.
- `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack --ran FILE`: "93 derived famil(ies) accounted for — 93 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED (a DERIVED zero — all 93 recorded an exit code and none of them is 3)". Exit 0.
- On the first pass (head `5fda11a5`), `check:system-context-census` was red: the new function reads `isSystem` and no row on `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx` owned it. Row 57 now does (commit `2020b6e5`). Two prerequisite exits on that pass were cleared and pass on the final run: the teardown-shape self-test's pinned fixture commit was fetched, and the CJS-load gate ran after the full build.
- Not measured locally, as `--commands` lists them: the families whose argv takes a value only a CI run has (`check-issue-citations.mjs --census`, the shard attestation emitters, `check-test-completeness.mjs`), and the CI-scheduled jobs (Build Core, Build Docs, the type-check lanes, and the `main`-only dogfood and temporal batteries). Those are CI's readings.

</details>

## Human Minimum

Each item is one rule from
[CONTRIBUTING.md › Human Minimum](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#human-minimum),
which links the AGENTS.md text that states it.

- [x] 1. Schemas start as Zod; `packages/spec` holds no runtime logic.
- [x] 2. Every name I added uses the casing for its kind.
- [x] 3. No formatter ran; `pnpm lint` passes.
- [x] 4. One issue, one branch off an up-to-date `main`, one pull request.
- [x] 5. A change that publishes carries a changeset, and both declaration lines are filled in here and in the changeset.
- [x] 6. `packages/spec` touched: its generated artifacts are regenerated and committed. (Not touched.)
- [x] 7. No hand edits to `content/docs/references/`, `packages/*/CHANGELOG.md` or `content/docs/releases/`.
- [x] 8. Title, body and comments are in English.
- [x] The *Before Submitting* list in CONTRIBUTING.md is done.
